text:
deploybot: Deploy started: inference-proxy v2.3.4 -> v2.3.5 (quick roll). Narrow smoke window (10m) enabled, cohort=dry-run. kicking off synth probes across eu-west-1 / us-west-2. watching route: /v1/generate. @sre please standby.

maya: saw a p95 jump on eu-west-1 at +2m: 1.9s (baseline ~0.45s). p50 steady ~120ms. no 5xxs. snapshot logs below.
```
[2026-03-21T00:02:14Z] host=eu-west-1-03 inference-proxy handler=generate latency=1900ms trace=trace-292345682
[2026-03-21T00:02:14Z] host=eu-west-1-04 worker=python-ingest GC=350ms
[2026-03-21T00:02:15Z] host=eu-west-1-03 cache=miss prefill=start
```

jorge: suggest holding rollout until we rule out prefill/GC. can we pin to model-variant=stable-quant for the dry-run cohort and re-run synths for +5m? also lower probe parallelism to 2.

liam: @maya can you share trace details for trace-292345682? I'll tail the worker logs and check host metrics (CPU, RQ length).

maya: trace uploaded: internal://traces/trace-292345682. quick look shows a ~350ms GC pause on two different hosts within same timeframe. not a network spike.

sre-runbook-bot: Runbook link: https://internal/runbooks/smoke-anomalies. Quick checklist: - confirm no client 5xx - confirm queue depth < 5 - confirm prefill warming completed - validate KV cache hit-rate. Start checks now.

deploybot: Rollout paused (manual) :pause_button: holding at 30% traffic for v2.3.5. Auto-rollback threshold: if p95 > 1.2s for 2 consecutive 2m windows then rollback to v2.3.4. Notifying release-owner @jorge.

jorge: +1 to pause. I'll open a hotfix PR to reduce prefill concurrency and add a small delay before heavy probes. ETA ~20m.

liam: if we need to rollback I can coordinate canary labels and force traffic back to stable after rollback. ping me once decision made. :thumbsup:

maya: monitoring update: p95 trending down after pause. at +7m p95 ~0.6s, p50 ~110ms. continuing to observe for remaining window.

deploybot: status update: smoke window extended +5m for extra coverage per request. keep logs and traces coming in this thread.
